nearest_prior_work: Fischler and Zudilin (2010), hypothesis (N) and Theorems A--B on printed p. 740, compare exponential small-form decay alpha with exponential coefficient height beta; their Theorem 2 on p. 742 improves the threshold using common divisors of coefficients.

Fischler and Rivoal (2010), Introduction and section 4.3, study integer linear forms with prescribed coefficient growth and form decrease and encode the comparison by the logarithmic ratio -log(alpha)/log(beta).
classification.attribution: Describe the general inequality as elementary Nesterenko-style effective-height/small-form bookkeeping. Cite Fischler--Zudilin for common-divisor reductions in effective coefficient height and Fischler--Rivoal for prescribed growth/decrease language. Credit the local card only for isolating the exact clearing decomposition used by this programme and for the conditional 3/2 specialization.
classification.mathematical_interest: The abstract inequality is elementary, but the card has real diagnostic value: it forces decay, rational-evaluation homogenisation, and proved coefficient clearing onto one degree scale before a construction is treated as viable.
classification.reusable_scope: The balance applies to any rational-evaluation construction with an independently proved decay estimate and an actual integral clearing bound. It is useful in Pade, Hermite--Pade, hypergeometric, q-hypergeometric, recurrence, and determinant constructions, but only after the family-specific rates are established.
classification.why_it_matters: It retires a recurrent reasoning error: nominal rank, number of functions, or order of vanishing does not by itself control the height of the cleared integer form. The conditional constant 0.107210739... is therefore a target for arithmetic efficiency, not evidence that a rank-three family exists.

mechanism_comparison.standard_core: An integer linear form can drive a Diophantine conclusion only when its smallness beats its effective integral coefficient height, together with the relevant nonvanishing and regularity hypotheses.
mechanism_comparison.local_generalization_delta: Before integrality, the card explicitly splits effective height into the b^D homogenisation cost of evaluation at a/b and an independently proved a^(kappa D) coefficient-clearing cost, then subtracts both from the decay exponent on the same D-scale.
mechanism_comparison.conditional_specialization: For an assumed rank-r family with lambda=r-1, algebra gives t<(r-1-kappa)/r. At q=3/2 and r=3 this is exactly kappa_3<2-3log(2)/log(3).
mechanism_comparison.negative_consumer: The cubic Hankel example shows why order alone is insufficient: cubic decay paired with cubic cost remains a fixed unfavorable ratio. The finite degree-3-through-12 solve is computational evidence only.
mechanism_comparison.significance_boundary: The card is a design and triage interface. It supplies neither a family, an integrality theorem, nonvanishing, an irrationality contradiction, nor a solution of Erdos Problem 1049.
